investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota or physical peer-pod VM slots are exhausted), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota or physical peer-pod VM slots are exhausted), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-30 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which report insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or exercising the runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. This is a cluster-capacity or node-resource constraint failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the observability eval infrastructure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

All three sibling checks show the same error, strongly pointing to a shared infrastructure constraint rather than an isolated eval bug.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. If the affinity rule is overly restrictive or the node pool has not been scaled, new pods cannot be placed even when the 2 eligible nodes have free general CPU/memory.

TERTIARY — Cluster node pool not scaled to meet concurrent eval demand: if multiple eval runs or production workloads were competing for the same 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes simultaneously, the resource pool could be transiently exhausted without a persistent capacity deficit.

LOWER — Eval runner scheduling a pod that requires a resource type (kata.peerpods.io/vm) that is not available in sufficient quantity for the eval environment: the eval may be targeting a node class that is intentionally limited in the production-api environment.
